title: On Zero-Shot Counterspeech Generation by LLMs
measurement_description: The paper measured the ability of Large Language Models to generate zero-shot counterspeech in response to hate speech. Some of the hate speech examples used for evaluation were targeted at religious groups, specifically Jews and Muslims. The evaluation also implicitly covered the models' use of religious identity (e.g., 'I am a Muslim') in the generated counterspeech.
findings: The study used hate speech targeting Jews and Muslims to evaluate counterspeech generation. It found that models like GPT-2, FlanT5, and especially ChatGPT were capable of generating relevant counterspeech. Some generated responses included assertions of religious identity (e.g., 'I am a Muslim,' 'I am a christian'). Notably, ChatGPT could generate fact-based counterspeech that referenced Islamic principles to counter hate speech against women.
